#### Key Factors That Drive a Children's Book's Value

- **First Edition, First Printing:** Later editions printed by the thousands are usually worth very little. You need to verify the copyright and printing number lines.
- **The Dust Jacket:** For 20th-century books, a missing dust jacket can slash a book’s value by 80% or more.
- **Inscriptions or Signatures:** An author's signature—or better yet, a personal inscription (like Mark Twain or J.K. Rowling writing to a specific person)—dramatically spikes the worth.
- **Condition:** Foxing (age spots), torn pages, missing color plates, or scribbled crayon marks from an actual child reading it will pull the value down.[[1]](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/rare-books/children/)[[2]](https://www.abebooks.com/books/rarebooks/most-valuable-childrens-books.shtml)

If you have a vintage or classic children's book sitting on your shelf, tell me the **title**, **year** , and **publisher listed on the copyright page** , and I can help you look up what specific edition you might have.
